  "business_value": "EConverter converts document handling from a manual, tool-fragmented chore into a governed platform capability. The primary value drivers are: (1) Cost and licensing consolidation — one system replaces separate converters, PDF editors, OCR tools and ad-hoc RAG scripts, with a converter catalog (IConverterCatalogService) that makes supported input/output pairs a first-class, discoverable product surface. (2) Confidentiality and data residency — documents are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM envelope encryption (per-document ephemeral DEK wrapped by a master KEK), access is scoped per owner at the aggregate level, and the retrieval/search core is designed to operate over locally indexed content, allowing regulated customers to keep document content on-premise. (3) Knowledge extraction at scale — OCR (Tesseract) plus semantic chunking, HNSW vector indexing, BM25 lexical retrieval, RRF fusion, MMR diversification and LLM reranking turn static document archives into answerable knowledge, with a reproducible benchmark harness (RagBenchmarkRunner reporting Recall, Precision, MRR, nDCG and faithfulness) acting as a shipping quality gate. (4) Defensible deliverables — CopilotDossierExporter produces publication-ready Executive Briefings, cross-document comparisons, clause diffs and audit dossiers in PDF, DOCX, XLSX and Markdown, converting internal analysis into artifacts executives, auditors and clients actually consume. (5) Operational resilience — the queue-backed worker model decouples long-running conversions from the interactive UI, with job attempts, priority, progress tracking, cancellation and batch-completion detection providing the observability enterprises require for heavy document workloads.",

  "architecture_summary": "EConverter is an enterprise-grade, self-hosted document conversion and document-intelligence platform implemented as a layered Clean Architecture .NET solution. The dependency graph is strictly inward-facing: Domain holds the aggregates and invariants (Document, User, ProcessingJob, Folder, DocumentVersion, AuditEvent, SystemSetting) with no outward references; Contracts carries outward-facing DTOs (Documents, Processing, Editor, AI, Admin, Messages); Application declares the use-case ports (IDocumentService, IProcessingService, IConverterCatalogService, IDocumentIntelligenceService, IPdfEngine, IAdminService, IDocumentStorage, IAuditService, IMalwareScanner, IUserContext) together with orchestration services such as DocumentService, DocumentIntelligenceService and DocumentService; Infrastructure supplies all concrete adapters (EF Core/PostgreSQL persistence, AES-256-GCM storage encryption, Tesseract OCR, PdfSharp/PdfPig/OpenXml conversion engines, HNSW and BM25 retrieval, RabbitMQ messaging, Tesseract/ClamAV integration); and the Web host acts as the single composition root (Program.cs) that binds every port to an adapter, configures the Blazor Server pipeline, SignalR hubs, hosted services, health checks and OpenTelemetry. Two executable hosts exist: DocumentConverter.Web (interactive Blazor UI plus REST endpoint surface under /documents, /api/documents, /api/processing and related routes) and DocumentWorker (a headless background consumer that executes the conversion lifecycle against the same Domain/Application/Infrastructure core through the shared DocumentConverter.Processing.Abstractions building block). Technology selection is deliberately privacy-oriented: PostgreSQL as the authoritative system of record, RabbitMQ as the asynchronous delivery layer, in-process HNSW vector indexes and a thread-safe BM25 inverted index for retrieval, and an optional provider-abstracting ExternalAiClient that normalises OpenAI, Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini dialects into one internal streaming contract.       "summary": "The AI directory is the domain-model layer for DocumentConverter's Copilot feature set, defining the persistent entities that back chat sessions, individual chat messages, long-term AI memory facts, and per-user Copilot preferences. All four files are sealed C# entities deriving from the shared Entity base class in DocumentConverter.Domain.Common, and they interoperate as an aggregate: a CopilotChatSession owns a collection of CopilotChatMessage objects, which can be promoted into CopilotMemoryItem records that are governed by CopilotUserSettings. It contains no infrastructure or I/O, but it is the canonical schema of the AI subsystem, so downstream persistence, application services, and API layers are all shaped by these definitions."

      "summary": "The Processing directory is the domain core of DocumentConverter's asynchronous conversion pipeline, holding the aggregate roots and domain entities that model batch jobs, converter registration, processing jobs, their retry attempts, input/output references, and the job lifecycle state machine. Files work together as a cohesive DDD domain layer: ProcessingJob orchestrates work and owns ProcessingAttempt/Input/Output children, BatchJob coordinates multi-document batches, Converter describes the available conversion backends, and ProcessingJobStatus defines the legal state transitions and structured error codes. It is a high-value backend (.NET/C#) business-logic hub with no external dependencies beyond the shared domain Common namespace."

      "subdirectory_count": 1,
      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: This directory is the AI/retrieval infrastructure layer of a .NET document-conversion backend, containing the lexical search engine (BM25 inverted index), background indexing pipeline (channel-based queue), and executive-report exporters (PDF/DOCX/XLSX/Markdown dossiers). The files work together as a cohesive RAG-style pipeline: documents are queued via DocumentIndexingChannel, indexed by Bm25InvertedIndex with IDF/field-boost/stemming, and the results are rendered into publication-ready deliverables by CopilotDossierExporter. This is core backend business logic with heavy algorithmic complexity, making it one of the highest-value areas of the project. The AI directory is the Application-layer intelligence hub of the DocumentConverter backend, housing the AI orchestration services that drive document analysis, indexing, and semantic extraction. It sits between the Documents/Storage layers and the Contracts/AI abstractions, wiring document access control, change-tracking, and global index upserts into streaming analysis pipelines. This batch captures the dominant file, DocumentIntelligenceService.cs, a ~6k-line sealed service that coordinates all AI document operations. This directory is the AI/RAG infrastructure layer of the DocumentConverter backend, implementing multilingual language detection, external LLM provider dispatch (OpenAI/Claude/Gemini), bilingual chunk projection, and a reproducible RAG benchmark harness. The files are cohesive service components that together power retrieval-augmented generation: detection feeds translation/chunking, chunking feeds the benchmark runner, and the external client provides LLM completion and reranking transport. High business value since it encapsulates the project's core AI differentiation with zero external tooling dependencies for the offline path. Core AI retrieval layer of the DocumentConverter backend, centered on the RAG retrieval orchestration pipeline (Components A–H) that combines LLM query understanding, HNSW vector search, fusion, and MMR reranking. This batch contains the largest and most business-critical file of the directory, which wires embedding search, chunk translation handling, and result validation into a single retrieval service. It is a hub-style infrastructure package consumed by the application layer."

      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: EF Core migration set for the DocumentConverter.Infrastructure.Persistence layer, defining and evolving the relational schema consumed by AppDbContext (identity schema, document vector chunks, intelligence indices, copilot chat/memory tables). Each migration ships as a pair: a `<Timestamp>_<Name>.cs` file holding the Up/Down schema operations plus an auto-generated `.Designer.cs` file holding the model snapshot and `BuildTargetModel`. The directory is pure data-layer infrastructure — it is the authoritative history of the database schema and every table, column and index the application depends on. This directory contains Entity Framework Core database migrations for the DocumentConverter application's Postgres/SQL persistence layer, including timestamped migration classes (Up/Down schema changes) and their auto-generated Designer snapshots plus the current AppDbContextModelSnapshot. Together they define the authoritative evolution of the DocumentVectorChunks table — adding tri-language chunk support (a Language column) and widening the Embedding column to a larger byte[] vector — and together form the source of truth for the database schema. It is pure backend data-layer infrastructure, not business logic, but it gates every persistence operation in the app."

      "summary": "This directory is the core document-processing engine of the DocumentConverter backend — a .NET/C# infrastructure layer implementing the concrete conversion, compression, OCR, and PDF manipulation processors behind the IDocumentProcessor abstraction. It contains processor implementations (image, OCR, office, PDF), orchestration services (ProcessingService), supporting analyzers (PdfCapabilityAnalyzer), and interactive estimators (CompressionEstimatorService). Every conversion job flows through one of these processors, making this a high-concentration hub deeply coupled to the Application, Domain, Contracts, Persistence, and Ocr layers."

      "subdirectory_count": 0,
      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: The Common directory holds shared Blazor (Razor) UI components for the DocumentConverter web front end — specifically a document picker dialog and its embedded Windows-Explorer-style file browser. These components act as reusable presentation widgets that are injected with application services (IDocumentService, DialogService, NotificationService) to browse, list, and select documents. The directory carries low-to-moderate architectural weight: it is pure frontend UI, containing no business logic or data-access code, so it depends on the Contracts/Application layers rather than being depended upon by them. The Common directory is a shared presentation-layer hub inside the DocumentConverter Web (Blazor) project, holding reusable Razor components that are embedded across multiple pages rather than routed directly. Files here compose application/contract AI and document abstractions into generic UI surfaces, so changes ripple across every consuming page. This batch exposes only a subset of the directory (one of three files), so cross-file assessment is partial."
    },

      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: The pdfjs directory is a vendored third-party asset folder under wwwroot/lib that holds Mozilla's minified PDF.js distribution. It contains no project-authored business logic; its sole role is to ship a browser-side PDF rendering engine that the ASP.NET Core frontend loads statically to display PDF documents. The files are build artifacts consumed as-is, not maintained or imported by backend code. This directory is a vendored build-asset folder for Mozilla's PDF.js, containing the minified web-worker bundle that renders and parses PDF documents off the main UI thread. The files are third-party artifacts — generated, minified, and unmodified — so they carry no project-specific business logic and exist only to support client-side PDF viewing. The directory's role is purely infrastructural: a static runtime dependency served to the browser, not a hub of imports or an application entry point. The pdfjs directory hosts the client-side PDF.js-based interactive editor engine for the Document Converter Platform. pdfEditor.js is a single large IIFE that attaches a full editing surface to window.pdfEditor, handling page rendering, tool modes, operation stacks (with undo/redo), drag/selection interaction, and .NET (Blazor) interop callbacks. It is a self-contained frontend feature engine consumed by the platform's editor UI rather than a shared library or data layer."
